title: TESS 2-minute data of 25,490 M dwarfs give two new transit candidates at 4.11 h and 5.51 h and limit 2-4 Earth-radius planets at 0.15-0.5 d to below 0.04% of stars
abstract:
Question: Do public TESS 2-minute light curves of M dwarfs contain transiting planets with periods of 0.15 d to 0.6 d that are not known, and how common are such planets? Most TESS searches start at 0.5 d.
Approach: We searched one sector (the most recent) of each of 25,490 TIC M dwarfs with TESS magnitude 12.5 or brighter (sectors 1 to 107) with a box least-squares search. Thresholds were SNR 9 and SDE 9. For the 948 stars above the thresholds, automated tests used up to six sectors (odd-even, secondary, shape, sector and transit depth consistency, size, repetition). We inspected the 17 survivors with transit fits, stellar-density checks, difference images, depth-aperture tests, Gaia neighbours and independent full-frame-image data. 3,000 injections measured the completeness of the search and automated tests.
Results: The search keeps 8 of 10 known confirmed planets in this period range. We report two new candidates. TIC 67502817.01 has P = 0.171172940 +/- 0.000000192 d (4.108 h), depth 598 ppm and radius 1.67 Earth radii around an early M dwarf at 93 pc. It is in five sectors (2020 to 2023, three cameras) with one linear ephemeris over 7,943 orbits. The transit-shape density agrees with the host (3.3 against 3.5 g/cm3), the shape is U-like, and the pixel data put the source on the target. If it is a planet, it has the shortest known period for a transiting planet around a main-sequence star and needs a density above about 9 g/cm3. TIC 63562537.01 has P = 0.2297 d (5.51 h), depth 260 ppm and radius 1.00 Earth radius around an early M dwarf at 42 pc. A blind search of independent 2024 full-frame data finds it again. We reject 5 other new signals as binaries, blends or pulsation and cannot resolve 1. For 0.15 d to 0.5 d, the rate of 1-2 Earth-radius planets is 0.17% per star (68% interval 0.12% to 0.25%), and the 95% upper limit for 2-4 Earth-radius planets is 0.035% at 88% completeness.
Limitations: One sector per star limits sensitivity to small planets. Completeness excludes the inspection step. TIC stellar parameters are approximate. The candidates need radial-velocity, high-resolution imaging and ground-based follow-up; for TIC 67502817.01 the Roche limit predicts a radial-velocity semi-amplitude of at least about 13 m/s.

Top right: S46 difference image in units of its error; the source is on the target (star), not on the Gaia neighbours (circles). Bottom left and centre: independent full-frame-image data of sectors 22 (2020) and 72 (2023) folded at the 2-minute ephemeris. Bottom right: transit times of five sectors against one linear ephemeris over 7,943 orbits.

TIC 63562537.01. Top left: sector 58 2-minute data folded at P = 0.22973 d with the transit model (Rp = 1.00 Earth radius). Top right: blind BLS search of independent sector 85 full-frame-image data; the top peak is at the sector-58 period (dotted line). Bottom left: sector 85 data folded at their own transit time, with the sector-58 model shape. Bottom right: sector 58 difference image in units of its error.

Left: SNR and SDE of the strongest BLS peak for the real flux of 25,490 stars and for the inverted flux of 3,768 stars, with the thresholds and the 10 planets kept. Centre: fraction of 3,000 injected planets recovered by the search and automated vetting, with the recovered known planets (circles) and the new candidates (stars). Right: planets per M dwarf for P = 0.15-0.5 d by radius (68% intervals; triangle: 95% upper limit with no detection).
